description: AG-1 Audit Intelligence Graph for GII GeM ERP. Catalogs the audit action catalog (events), source modules, data mutation boundaries, actor roles, approval flows, compliance controls, critical actions, audit stores and trust boundaries. Built read-only from the audit trail implementation; contains no live business data.

graphReferences.role: Declares audit_log, allocation_audit and voucher_proposal_audit table structures
Approval and closure stages (approval submit/approve, order closure) are audit-observable lifecycle events
Voucher posting and reversal actions are the highest-severity accounting audit events
Renderer IPC channels that originate audit entries (audit:context, document view/download)
User-facing modules and business rules referenced by audit modules
Metadata and permissions context for actor roles and trust boundaries
The Audit Watch guide (audit-watch-guide) is generated from the same catalogue as detectiveControls

auditStores.purpose: Primary generic audit trail for every audited action across modules.
auditStores.integrityMechanism: SHA-256 event_hash over serialized event body (created_at included)

auditStores.purpose: Receipt/payment/advance allocation change trail. Every write is mirrored to audit_log as 'allocation <action>'.
auditStores.integrityMechanism: Mirror write into audit_log preserves the generic trail

auditStores.purpose: Bank reconciliation voucher proposal lifecycle (generate → edit → approve/reject → draft voucher → voucher posted).
auditStores.integrityMechanism: Terminal events are additionally mirrored into audit_log (voucher_proposal_posted)

complianceControls.name: Audit event hash integrity
complianceControls.mechanism: SHA-256 event_hash computed over serialized event body including created_at at insert time

complianceControls.name: Audit log protected write policy
complianceControls.mechanism: audit_log placed in accounting read-only write-policy set; generic CRUD cannot write directly

complianceControls.name: Health center audit log check
complianceControls.mechanism: audit_log table presence verified; zero-row trail raises warning before production use

complianceControls.name: Critical action audit coverage gate
complianceControls.mechanism: verify-controls asserts critical actions (permission_denied, bulk import, rollback import, voucher reversal) are present in audit_log

complianceControls.name: Financial statement report audit evidence
complianceControls.mechanism: FSR verifiers assert inventory GL postings, year close and account mapping audit evidence exists

complianceControls.name: Audit store reset protection
complianceControls.mechanism: audit_log, voucher_proposal_audit and allocation_audit are excluded from operational reset wipe list

complianceControls.name: Delete-safety enforcement
complianceControls.mechanism: hard_delete flows through assertDeleteSafe with old_value capture; sensitive tables blocked

trustBoundaries.note: Renderer can write arbitrary audit entries by design; treat as a controlled trust boundary.
Audited with null user_id in some paths — unattributed actor coverage gap.
Proposal lifecycle stored separately; terminal events mirrored into audit_log.
Allocation trail always mirrored into the generic audit_log.

knownGaps.gap: Several audit paths record null user_id (document view/download; some crudHelpers deletes), weakening actor resolution.
voucher_proposal_audit records are not mirrored into audit_log except terminal posting events; intermediate proposal edits are only visible in the proposal store.
The generic audit:context IPC channel allows renderer-originated audit writes; acceptable by design but should be reviewed for spoofing risk.
Audit graph is descriptive; no runtime consumer yet maps live audit_log rows to graph event IDs.

validationRules: All event IDs must be unique.
Every critical event must also appear in criticalActions.
Every event must reference a module present in modules.
Every event action must map to a documented severity.
All mutations must reference a known table and classify mutation severity.
All approval stages must reference known audit actions.
The graph must not contain live business data (no real record ids, user ids, or transaction values).
All sourceDocuments paths must resolve to existing files.
metadata counts must match the arrays they describe.
statistics counts must match the eventCatalog severity distribution.
The graph must remain read-only; regeneration is the only permitted mutation path.
AG-1 must be registered in repository/graph-registry.json as Active.

risk.description: Audit trail is implemented with tamper-evident hashing and write-policy protection, but actor attribution is incomplete in a few paths and the renderer audit write channel is a controlled trust boundary.

futureExtensions: Runtime mapping of live audit_log rows to AG-1 event IDs for the Health Center and Help Assistant.
Anomaly detection over audit events (e.g., reversal bursts, repeated failed logins, after-hours postings).
Cross-graph audit lineage: event → module → screen (RG-1) → table (DG-1) → workflow stage (WG-1).
Tamper-evident audit chain with previous-hash linkage for stronger compliance evidence.
Attribution hardening for unattributed actor paths (document view/download and generic deletes).
Proposal audit mirroring so voucher_proposal_audit intermediate events also appear in audit_log.

checks.title: Same supplier bill entered twice

limits.label: Same amount counts as a repeat within this many days

checks.meaning: Two purchase bills from one supplier carry the same bill number in the same financial year (ignoring spaces, dashes, slashes, dots and case), or two bills of the same amount within a few days of each other (each such pair is shown once). Reversed bills do not count, and placeholders such as NA or 0 are not treated as bill numbers. The supplier could be paid twice for one supply.
checks.nextStep: Open both bills and compare them with the supplier's bill copy. Delete the duplicate if it was keyed twice.

checks.title: Same supplier paid twice

limits.label: Same amount counts as a repeat within this many days

checks.meaning: Two supplier payments carry the same UTR, or the same supplier was paid the same amount twice within a few days (each such pair is shown once). Reversed payments do not count, and short placeholders such as NA or CASH are not treated as UTRs.
checks.nextStep: Check the bank statement. If the money left twice, ask the supplier for a refund or adjust the next bill.

checks.title: Supplier paid soon after its bank account changed

limits.label: Flag payments made within this many days of the change

checks.meaning: A supplier's bank account number, IFSC, bank name or UPI id was changed and the supplier was paid soon after. A changed account is the usual route for misdirected payments. Changes made in bulk through Master Data Tools are not linked to later payments yet; Sensitive master change (AW-T04) lists those batches.
checks.nextStep: Confirm the new account with the supplier by phone on a number already on file, not one from the change request.

checks.title: Supplier paid more than billed

limits.label: Ignore differences up to this amount

checks.meaning: Payments and advances set against a purchase bill add up to more than the bill. The extra is either an advance that belongs to another bill, or an overpayment.
checks.nextStep: Move the extra to the right bill or record it as an advance; ask for a refund of any overpayment.

checks.title: Purchases split to stay under a limit

limits.label: The company's purchase approval limit
A bill counts as near the limit from this share of it
Bills within this many days count together
Flag this many near-limit bills or more

checks.meaning: Several bills from one supplier within a week each sit just under the approval limit, while together they are over it.
checks.nextStep: Ask who approved the purchases and whether one order was split. Set the limit to the company's real approval limit.

checks.title: Unusual purchase rate

limits.label: Flag rates this far above the item's median
Median taken over this many days
Need at least this many earlier purchases of the item

checks.meaning: An item was bought well above the median rate the company paid for it over the past year.
checks.nextStep: Check for a genuine reason (urgent order, different model, price rise) and keep the note with the bill.

checks.title: One bank account shared by two parties
checks.meaning: Two suppliers, or a supplier and an employee, have the same bank account number and IFSC. Money paid to one may reach the other.
checks.nextStep: Ask both parties for a cancelled cheque or bank letter and correct the master that is wrong.

checks.title: Payment to a supplier with no GSTIN or marked inactive

limits.label: Flag payments from this amount

checks.meaning: A sizeable payment went to a supplier that has no GSTIN on file or is marked inactive. Input GST cannot be claimed without the GSTIN, and an inactive supplier should not be receiving money.
checks.nextStep: Collect the GSTIN or confirm the supplier is unregistered; reactivate the supplier only if the payment is genuine.

checks.title: Purchase order, goods receipt and bill do not agree

limits.label: Allowed difference between the three documents

checks.meaning: The quantity or value on the supplier bill differs from the purchase order or the goods actually received (three-way match).
checks.nextStep: Waits for the purchase-order work (ACC P-01) to reach the main build.

checks.title: Sold below cost or well below the quoted rate

limits.label: Flag billing this far below the quoted rate

checks.meaning: An item was billed below what it cost to buy and deliver, or well below the rate quoted on the order.
checks.nextStep: Check the order terms and any approved discount; correct the bill if the rate was keyed wrongly.

checks.title: Credit note dated after the bill's period
checks.meaning: A credit note reduces a sales bill from an earlier month or financial year. Late credit notes move income between periods and need GST return care.
checks.nextStep: Confirm the reason and that the credit note is reported in the right GST return.

checks.title: Bill keyed late or dated before delivery

limits.label: Flag bills keyed this many days after their date

checks.meaning: A sales bill was entered well after its bill date (backdating), or carries a date before the goods were dispatched (cut-off).
checks.nextStep: Check the dates against the GeM portal and the challan. Income must fall in the period the goods were supplied.

checks.title: Receivable overdue past its credit terms

limits.label: Credit days when a bill has no due date and no terms are set for the buyer
Flag bills more than this many days past their due date

checks.meaning: A sales bill is still unpaid well after its due date. The due date already includes the buyer's credit days and grace period.
checks.nextStep: Follow up with the department; check for a pending CRAC or deduction that is holding the payment.

checks.title: GeM contract billed twice or billed above the order
checks.meaning: The same GeM contract number appears on bills for two different orders, or more quantity was billed than the order contains.
checks.nextStep: Compare with the GeM contract. Cancel the extra bill or raise a credit note.

checks.title: More received than billed

limits.label: Ignore differences up to this amount

checks.meaning: Receipts and deductions against a bill add up to more than the bill. Either a receipt went to the wrong bill or a refund is due.
checks.nextStep: Reallocate the receipt to the right bill, or record the refund due to the buyer.

checks.title: Large deduction by the buyer

limits.label: Flag other deductions above this share of the bill

checks.meaning: The buyer kept back a large amount as 'other deductions' (not TDS or GST TDS), such as a penalty or short payment.
checks.nextStep: Get the department's deduction letter. Claim it back if it is wrong, or book it to the right expense.

checks.title: Negative stock
checks.meaning: The stock register shows less than zero of an item in a warehouse. The posting guards should stop this, so a hit means stock went out before it was received or a guard was bypassed.
checks.nextStep: Find the inward entry that is missing or late and record it with its real date.

checks.title: Slow-moving stock

limits.label: Flag items with stock and no movement for this many days

checks.meaning: An item has stock on hand but has not moved for months, including opening stock that has never moved. Money is tied up and the stock may be obsolete.
checks.nextStep: Plan to use, return or sell the stock; consider writing down its value at year end.

checks.title: Large or frequent stock adjustments

limits.label: Flag one adjustment from this value
Flag an item adjusted this many times
Repeats counted within this many days

checks.meaning: Stock was adjusted by a large value (the value actually posted, which for a write-off keyed without a rate is the average cost), or the same item was adjusted again and again. Adjustments change stock without a supplier or buyer document.
checks.nextStep: Check the reason and the physical count sheet for each adjustment.

checks.title: Many damaged returns from one supplier

limits.label: Flag a supplier with this many damaged returns
Counted over this many days

checks.meaning: A supplier's goods keep coming back damaged or defective.
checks.nextStep: Review the supplier's quality and claim credit notes for every damaged return.

checks.title: Serial number used twice
checks.meaning: The same serial number of an item is recorded more than once. One physical unit cannot be bought or delivered twice.
checks.nextStep: Check the unit's label and correct the wrong entry.

checks.title: Expired batch still in stock
checks.meaning: A batch past its expiry date still shows quantity on hand.
checks.nextStep: Remove expired stock from saleable stock and record the write-off.

checks.title: Bought more than the order needs, or billed more than delivered

limits.label: Allowed excess over the order

checks.meaning: More was purchased against an order line than the order asks for, or more was billed on an order than was delivered on confirmed delivery challans. Orders that use no delivery challan are not compared.
checks.nextStep: Find where the extra stock went, or hold the bill until delivery is complete.

checks.title: Hand-made journal to a sensitive ledger

limits.label: Flag journals from this amount

checks.meaning: A journal typed by hand (a manual voucher, or a journal or contra keyed through Guided Vouchers) moves money in cash or bank, capital, GST or a suspense ledger, judged by each ledger's account group. These ledgers normally move only through receipts, payments and bills.
checks.nextStep: Read the narration and supporting paper; make sure a second person approved it.

checks.title: Entry on a Sunday or outside office hours

limits.label: Office opens (IST)
Office closes (IST)

checks.meaning: A voucher is dated on a Sunday, or was keyed outside office hours. Not wrong in itself, but entries made when nobody is watching deserve a second look.
checks.nextStep: Confirm who made the entry and why it could not wait.

checks.title: Round-sum journal

limits.label: Flag from this amount
Amount is an exact multiple of this

checks.meaning: A large journal is an exact round figure. Real transactions rarely land on round sums; estimates and plugs often do.
checks.nextStep: Ask for the calculation behind the figure.

checks.title: Suspense or clearing balance left open

limits.label: Flag balances older than this

checks.meaning: A suspense or clearing ledger (such as Opening Balance Suspense or Goods Received Not Invoiced) still holds a balance from more than a month ago. These ledgers should empty out.
checks.nextStep: Clear each old item to its proper ledger.

checks.title: Backdated voucher
coverage: any voucher posted into a closed year

limits.label: Flag vouchers dated this many days before they were keyed

checks.meaning: A voucher whose date a person chose carries a date well before the day it was keyed, or any voucher was entered into a year after it was closed. Backdating can push income or expense into a period that was already reported. Bills and payments that take their document's date are not counted; late sales bills are AW-S03's.
checks.nextStep: Confirm the real transaction date and that reports already filed are not affected.

checks.title: Many reversals, or reversal of an old voucher

limits.label: A reversal this long after the voucher date is late
Flag a user with this many reversals
Reversals counted within this many days

checks.meaning: A voucher was reversed long after its date, or one user reversed many vouchers in a short time.
checks.nextStep: Check each reason; repeated reversals point to a training gap or a process being worked around.

checks.title: Bank line left unmatched

limits.label: Flag lines unmatched for this many days

checks.meaning: A line from an imported bank statement is not in the books: it was neither matched, booked through a voucher proposal, nor reconciled. A suggested match nobody confirmed still counts as open.
checks.nextStep: Match it in Bank Reconciliation, or record the missing receipt, payment or bank charge.

checks.title: First digits do not follow the usual pattern

limits.label: Run only on ledgers with this many entries
Flag when the first-digit spread differs by more than this (MAD x 1000)

checks.meaning: In natural business amounts, about 30% start with 1 and fewer start with each higher digit (Benford's law). A ledger whose amounts break that pattern may have invented or repeated figures.
checks.nextStep: Look at the digits that are over-represented and sample those entries.

checks.title: Cash in hand below zero
checks.meaning: On some day a cash-in-hand ledger shows more paid out than ever came in. Cash-in-hand means a ledger in the cash group other than a bank, or, for a ledger with no group, an asset ledger whose name says cash (such as Petty Cash). A balance that was already below zero when the period starts is shown too. Physical cash cannot go negative, so a receipt is missing or a payment is wrong.
checks.nextStep: Find the cash receipt that should come before the payment and record it with its real date.

checks.title: Book integrity
checks.meaning: The existing book checks: the trial balance ties, every voucher balances, no posting is stuck, and the audit trail's hash chain is unbroken. Negative stock and over-collected bills are shown by AW-I01 and AW-S06 instead, so they are not counted twice.
checks.nextStep: Open Error Console for the details.

checks.title: Admin account unused for a long time

limits.label: Flag admin accounts unused for this many days

checks.meaning: An active admin or super admin account has not logged in for months. Unused powerful accounts are easy to misuse.
checks.nextStep: Disable the account, or confirm who still needs it.

checks.title: Repeated failed logins or locked account

limits.label: Flag accounts with this many failed attempts

checks.meaning: Someone keeps entering the wrong password for an account, or the account is locked.
checks.nextStep: Ask the user whether it was them. Reset the password if not.

checks.title: Maker and approver are the same person
checks.meaning: One user both prepared (keyed or submitted) and approved the same voucher or record, so the second check never happened.
checks.nextStep: Have another user review it. If the company runs with one user, record that decision.

checks.title: Sensitive master change

limits.label: Show changes from this many days

checks.meaning: Bank details or an employee's incentive percentage were changed, one record at a time or in bulk through Master Data Tools. A user's role raised to admin is also shown once the app records role changes; it does not record them yet.
checks.nextStep: Confirm each change was requested and approved.

checks.title: Audit trail gap

limits.label: Look at actions from this many days

checks.meaning: Changes to records were logged without the user who made them, so they cannot be traced to a person.
checks.nextStep: Tell the developers; the screen or import that wrote these rows must record the user.

checks.title: Accounting policy setting changed
checks.meaning: A company-level accounting policy (such as maker-checker or single-user mode) was changed.
checks.nextStep: Waits for the accounting policy settings (ACC P-18) to reach the main build.
